  - `obj.unknownProp` where `obj` is an untyped parameter

if (n.isGetProp() &&

The most suspicious method is `com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeValidator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(...)`.

Why:
- Both failing tests are missing expected warnings on property access:
  - `x.prop` where `x` is `null`
  - `obj.unknownProp` where `obj` is an untyped parameter
- In `TypeCheck.visitGetProp`, property access diagnostics are gated by:
  - first calling `validator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(...)`
  - then only if that returns `true`, calling `checkPropertyAccess(...)`
- The helper contains this special-case suppression:

```java
if (n.isGetProp() &&
    !t.inGlobalScope() && type.isNullType()) {
  return true;
}
```

This is highly suspicious because it suppresses the exact null-property-access warning that `testGetprop4()` expects. The exception is broad: any non-global `GETPROP` on exact `null` skips reporting.

Static diagnosis:
- `TypeCheck.visitGetProp(...)` itself is structured correctly: it relies on `expectNotNullOrUndefined(...)` to decide whether to emit the “No properties on this expression” warning.
- The bug is that `TypeValidator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(...)` suppresses this warning in cases where it should not.
- That same suppression can also interfere with later missing-property checks by allowing invalid property accesses to proceed under the wrong assumptions, which is consistent with `testIssue810()` also losing its expected warning.

So the buggy method is:

`com.google.javascript.jscomp.TypeValidator.expectNotNullOrUndefined(com.google.javascript.jscomp.NodeTraversal, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType, java.lang.String, com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype.JSType)`
